editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 27 September
editions.lede: Afghanistan has been rerouted. The country now buys its flour, its fuel and its electricity through doors that did not matter five years ago.

items.headline: Pakistan promised to reopen the border. Then it shot at Spin Boldak.
items.gist: Shut since Oct 2025; fire exchanged 25 Sep; FY26 transit 11,592 containers ($367m) v 102,886 in FY23

items.headline: Kabul spent the week shopping in every direction but south.

editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 4 October
editions.lede: The rain is coming back. The money to use it is not.

items.headline: A wet winter arrives, and farmers cannot pay for the fertiliser
items.gist: El Niño-driven wetter winter expected as planting opens in October; fertiliser is the binding cost

items.headline: Most people sent home have not worked in a month
items.gist: IOM survey of 1,547 undocumented returnees: 69% of those 14+ had not worked in the previous 30 days

items.headline: Kabul puts up the duty on paint, plaster and plastic shoes
items.gist: 28 Sep tariff committee: paint 16% to 30%, plastic footwear and plaster 50% to 80%

items.headline: A million dollars against a banking system that barely lends
items.gist: 27 Sep central bank deal with Afghan Credit Guarantee Foundation: about $1m in grants to five banks and one microfinance lender
